newsitem.title: USA: Redhook Ale sees Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Redhook Ale sees Q1 loss.

text.p: Redhook Ale Brewery Inc on Friday said it would report a loss for the first quarter of 1997 due to disappointing sales and operating costs of a new brewery in Portsmourth, New Hampshire.
In a statement, the company said first quarter sales volume totaled 51,400 barrels, up a mere 3.4 percent from 49,700 barrels shipped 1996's first quarter.

Analysts had expected the company to report a profit of $0.01 per share for the first quarter ended March 30, 1997, according to investment research firm First Call. One year ago, the company earned a profit of $0.10 a share.

"The slowing growth rate that Redhook experienced in late 1996 has continued into 1997, although trends are positive in many regions of the country," Paul Shipman, chief executive, said in a statement.

Sales were up over 20 percent versus the first quarter of 1996 when shipments to states in the western United States are excluded. Shipments to the West Coast states declined 5.9% compared to the first quarter of 1996, the company said.
The Portsmouth brewery began operations during 1996's fourth quarter, and the rise in fixed and semi-variable costs associated with operating it increased cost of goods sold.
Also, the Portsmouth operation saw lower-than-expected sales volume.
Redhook will report its quarterly results as scheduled on April 29, 1997.
